title: Recipients to whom a pharmacist at a hospital or clinic pharmacy without a Drug Store pharmacy license may dispense
rule_summary: Under 247 CMR 9.01(13), unless otherwise permitted by law, a pharmacist connected with, or employed by, a hospital or clinic pharmacy that does not hold a Drug Store pharmacy license may not dispense drugs to any person other than inpatients or outpatients of the hospital or clinic, or to employees of said hospital or clinic, or to said employees' spouses and children who live in the same household with said employees.
exam_relevance: Tests the closed list of recipients, the same-household condition attached to an employee's spouse and children, the pharmacist as the person the paragraph addresses, and the opening words that yield to what other law permits.

authority.name: Massachusetts Board of Registration in Pharmacy regulations

exceptions: Dispensing to another person where it is otherwise permitted by law
common_confusions: The family members named are an employee's spouse and children, and only those who live in the same household with the employee.
The paragraph is addressed to a pharmacist connected with, or employed by, the hospital or clinic pharmacy, and it applies where that pharmacy does not hold a Drug Store pharmacy license.
The paragraph lists recipients and says nothing about who wrote the prescription.
verification_notes: Read on 2026-09-16 in the Board of Registration in Pharmacy's publication of 247 CMR 9.00 on mass.gov (PDF, Mass. Register #1536, 12/6/2024).
